newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate jumps to 11.6 vs 9.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate jumps to 11.6 vs 9.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate jumped to 11.6 percent on Friday from 9.1 percent after lenders raised most prices and imposed extra charges.
They cashed in on a strong pre-Christmas demand for kuna funds, totalling 53 million against very little money on offer.
New loans totalled 16.5 million kuna and creditors also agreed to roll over another 9.0 million.
The weighted call money rate rose to 10.5 from 9.0 percent recently. Insurance firms and banks granted one-week loans at 10 and 11 percent respectively, also up one percentage point.

As pressure to exchange hard currency for kuna ahead of holidays increased, its midrates calculated by the central bank continued to firm to 5.5309 against the dollar and 3.5548 the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
